extracted.intended_audience: housewives / practical housekeepers; mothers and young married women
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for women on household management, personal presentation, and domestic priorities — practical rules and moral counsel for the wife/housekeeper. Focuses on system, small duties, hospitality, and restraint in speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospitality that does not impose
rubrics_metrics.description: It is your duty to have things so nice every day, and always, that you cannot be too much 'put out' by an occasional guest. When you invite your friend to make you a visit, explain that you live quietly, and that he will find a warm welcome. Then give him just what you give John, and make no apologies. Above all, do not let him feel that any additional labor caused by his presence throws the whole course of the household machinery out of gear. Do not invite to your home those for whom you have to make so great a change in your daily life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell guests in advance about the household's ordinary ways; provide the normal household fare and welcome without apology; avoid invitations that require large, disruptive preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematize work (METHOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: First and foremost, Mary must learn to systematize her work. Method and management do wonders toward saving time and money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt routines and organize tasks so that work flows without hurry; compare calm, methodical housekeepers (who have time for sewing and reading) with hurried ones whose work is never done.

rubrics_metrics.name: View domestic labor as ennobling
rubrics_metrics.description: I hope the young housekeepers to whom this talk is addressed will not consider such trifles as I have mentioned, degrading. It is the work laid before them and consequently cannot be mean. Such labor, when sweetened by the thought of what it all means, is ennobling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a dignified attitude toward everyday tasks; find moral/affective purpose in domestic work rather than shame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain personal appearance for husband's sake
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a wife's duty to study to look well in her husband's eyes, always and in all circumstances. Her person should be scrupulously clean, her hair becomingly arranged, her working-gown as neat as she can keep it, and relieved before John comes in by clean collar or ruching and a smooth white apron.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when doing her own work a woman should keep herself neat and add small finishing touches before her husband arrives to preserve personal courtesy and attractiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical and serviceable home attire
rubrics_metrics.description: As the months wear on...Dark prints and ginghams, simply made, and freshened up at meal-times by full white aprons, are serviceable, sensible, economical and significant of our dear Mary's practical wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor durable, easy-care fabrics for daily wear and reserve fine apparel for occasions; manage the trousseau to make garments last rather than hastily replacing costly things.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not let thrift be misconstrued as indifference
rubrics_metrics.description: In the honorable dread of suggesting to him whose fortune she has elected to share...she devises excuses for sparing the costly fabrics—pretexts which, to his shame it is said, he is prone to misunderstand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that husband may misinterpret necessary economy; communicate motives and maintain pride in careful stewardship to avoid misjudgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to small, unnoticed household details ('chink-fillers')
rubrics_metrics.description: The chink-fillers are among the most useful members of society...She it is who...picks up the hat or gloves Mamie has carelessly left...wipes the tiny finger smears from the window-panes...mends the ripped coat...remembers to prepare some dainty for that member of the household who is 'not quite up to the mark' in appetite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value and perform the unobtrusive, minute tasks (darning, wiping, tacking, removing basting-threads, preparing small comforts) that prevent embarrassment and keep family life harmonious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide the dainty, lady-like finishing touches (supplement servants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hireling cannot grasp the importance of the lesser tasks...Your servant may do the rough work; the dainty, lady-like touch must be given by you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervise and supplement hired help by adding the finishing inspections and touches servants tend to miss (cleaning soap-dishes, checking for tiny defects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate dining and household minutiae
rubrics_metrics.description: Other little cares are to ascertain that the water with which the tea is made is boiling, that the alcohol lamp is filled, the flies brushed from the room, the plates warmed, and the sugar-dishes and salt-cellars filled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the small practical elements of a meal/service in advance to avoid awkward pauses and interruptions when the family gathers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage household members to return things to place
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be an excellent plan for each member of the household to resolve to put in its proper place everything which he or she observed out of order. By the time this rule had been established for twenty-four hours, the house would be immaculate...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute simple household rules so every member helps maintain order, reducing repetitive corrective labor for the housekeeper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set priorities: something must be 'crowded out'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Something must be crowded out.' Certain duties are of prime importance, others only secondary...To the young mother this is, or should be, the first and great object in life. Her baby must have enough clothes...Home duties take the precedence of social engagements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately choose what to omit when time is limited: prioritize children, essential home duties, and health over social show or nonessential tasks; use a 'test-stone' (e.g., John's or baby's needs) to rank duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value thoroughness ('staying power') over rapid slovenliness
rubrics_metrics.description: She has a jaunty knack of pinning trimming on a hat...But it is an obvious fact that the work of this remarkable woman lacks 'staying power.' Her too rapid and long stitches often give way...The maker of gown, hat, preserves, and cake lacks thoroughness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sacrificing durability and quality for speed; prefer slower, careful work that lasts to rapid makeshift solutions that 'tumble to pieces.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate on one task; use system and routine
rubrics_metrics.description: The two great points in the successful management of time are concentration and system. At the beginning of each day set duties in array before your mind's eye, and attack them, one at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan the day, pick the most important task first, and persist until it is finished; resist stopping mid-task for less-important interruptions that fragment the day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve rest and health as essential duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Another thing which must not be crowded out is rest, and the care of the health,--and the one includes the other. A day in which no breathing-space has been found is a wicked day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard time for rest; avoid chronic overwork which harms disposition and productivity and is 'wretched economy' in the long run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary talking and gossip
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the things which may be easily and advantageously crowded out, we may rank unnecessary talking...Gossip is their meat and drink...When you work, work; and when you play, play, is an excellent motto for both mistress and maid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit idle conversation among servants and self; enforce focused work hours to prevent wasted time and diminished household efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply 'cui bono?' — consider usefulness before speaking or acting
rubrics_metrics.description: Thus I translate the Latin cui bono...The enterprise that led to no good was not worth beginning...What good will it do?...It is a very melancholy and most unsatisfactory satisfaction to know that you have made a person uncomfortable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before uttering harsh words or engaging in gossip/criticism, ask 'What good will it do?' Favor restraint: to repress a harsh answer, to confess a fault, and to stop in gentle submission are efforts that preserve domestic happiness. 'If you cannot say a kind thing say nothing.'
